Conflict Intelligence Platform · analysis layer

Every analytic method, run against the live corpus.

The Monitor dashboard, the Copilot taking a question from plain English to an executed analysis, the six calibrated capabilities run through the shipped dashboard with their limits printed in the frame, then all 28 methods in the platform's analysis catalog, run against the production stores over a single 2026-05-17 to 2026-06-30 window, each shown with the visualization it produces. Nothing here is a mock-up or a fixture: every figure is the output of a real query against real data.

The dashboard

What an analyst sees before running anything.

3

landing.monitor

live

The whole dashboard on first load: what the platform knows, where it happened, and what came in.

Three endpoints in one view. The banner under the map is the honesty rule in force -- it names the display cap and the text-only remainder rather than quietly showing a subset. The basemap is served from the same origin: the capture fails if the page contacts an external tile host.

landing.map

live

Events clustered by location and coloured by severity.

Clusters are countable and clickable; colour follows the severity scale, not the child count.

landing.windowed

live

The same dashboard narrowed to the last 90 days.

Narrowing the window drops the Levant cluster from 4,192 to 3,606 events and turns the summary into deltas. The control offers only spans relative to today, so against a corpus ending 2026-06-30 the 7-day and 30-day options return an empty dashboard.

The Copilot

Everything above assumes the analyst knows which method to run. This is what happens when they just ask.

2

guided

guided

A question the catalog can answer, taken from sentence to approved plan to executed analysis.

“Which actors were most active in the conflict between 17 May 2026 and 30 June 2026, and how did the volume of events change over that period?”

Turns
3
Wall clock
32.5s
Methods executed
temporal.event_count_series, actor.degree_centrality
Model
openai/gpt-5.6-luna
Report label
reproducible

The analyst asked a question in plain English. Before anything runs, the Copilot says back what it understood and stops. This is the difference between an analysis tool and a chatbot: no method executes until a person agrees the question was read correctly.

The proposed plan, named method by method, with its own limits stated before approval rather than buried in the result: it can rank actors by network connectedness, and it says outright that connectedness is not the same as activity, so the answer will be partial.

Both gates cleared, both methods run. The two rows between the turns are the run log — real catalog methods with their output types, the same ones an analyst could have picked by hand. The report closes by warning that the two results carry different data-as-of dates.

The Lab after the plan ran: catalog on the left, the result on the canvas, the conversation on the right. The analyst never opened the catalog.

research

research

A question the catalog cannot answer — the case where a system that wants to look capable would invent something.

“What is the average rainfall in the conflict zone, and does weather predict escalation between 17 May 2026 and 30 June 2026?”

Turns
3
Wall clock
29.2s
Methods executed
temporal.event_anomaly_raw
Model
openai/gpt-5.6-luna
Report label
reproducible

Asked about rainfall — which the platform holds no data for — the Copilot does not improvise. It states that no registered method covers the question, that anything it does next is exploratory and not reproducible, and re-badges itself Exploratory before asking to continue.

Approved, it composes the closest catalog method it has — daily event anomalies — and reports on that instead, saying plainly what the substitute cannot answer. One defect is visible here: the published report is labelled reproducible, contradicting the announcement it just made (#996).

The calibrated capabilities

Six methods whose thresholds were fitted on the corpus, not typed in. Each was run through the shipped dashboard on 25 August 2026 and photographed with its limits in the same frame.

6 + 1 gate

Every threshold below was chosen by a sweep whose decision rule was written down before any result was seen, and the sweep record stays on disk. Each figure reproduces its published fit exactly. All six ran against a read-only snapshot of the production data (data as of 2026-08-23, coverage through 2026-06-30), at zero cost: no paid call, no model, no write to any store. Nothing here is a statement about the live stores or about anything after 30 June.

escalation_detection

3 days flagged

Which days behaved like escalation: daily counts scored against a 21-day trailing baseline, a 7-day acceleration test and a source-composition check.

Found
3 escalation days: 7, 8 and 9 June 2026
Coverage
45 of 45 days carry sourced events (1.0 against a 0.75 floor)
Rejected by the check
29 and 30 June: surge and accelerate, but on sources absent from their own baseline
Fitted on
cal_2, #1004, 45-day window

The caveat in the frame is the rule in one line: a change in who is reporting is not a change in the world. The three days are days whose reporting volume behaved like escalation on this corpus, not a verdict on the world, and nothing is claimed past 30 June, where coverage stops.

actor_centrality_ranking

592 ranked

Who sits in the middle of the network: a composite of betweenness, PageRank and degree over actors with at least two relationship types.

Found
592 actors ranked of 2,965
Completeness
0.1997 against a 0.5 floor: the capability reports that it does not meet its own bar
Window
Not applied: actor-to-actor edges carry no dates, so this is the full materialised network
Fitted on
cal_3, #1005 and the #1056 re-fit

It ranks a fifth of the network and says so above the figure rather than presenting the fifth as the whole. The rendered table shows one row (rank 1, United States); the other 591 are in the data behind Show data. That clipping is a shared renderer issue recorded for a decision, not hidden.

actor_network_clustering

48 clusters

Who coordinates with whom: Louvain communities over the weighted coordination graph, opposition edges excluded so coordination stays distinct from opposition.

Found
48 clusters covering 982 actors
Modularity
0.73657 against a 0.3 minimum: meets the bar
Drawn
1,180 actors returned, 300 kept by the render cap, 100 drawn; 4 of 13 hulls hidden as too scattered to outline, all stated on the surface
Fitted on
cal_4, #1006

The picture is a capped sample of the published partition and the canvas says so. The modularity figure lives in the result envelope and is not yet rendered on any screen; putting it in the frame is a UI decision on the list.

geospatial_hotspot_analysis

88 hotspots

Where events concentrate: kernel-density hotspots at 2 km bandwidth with at least 9 events each, classified persistent or spike.

Found
88 hotspots over 5,160 plottable events; 3,468 captured inside a hotspot (0.6721)
Largest / median
525 events / 13 events
Plottable
50.7% of the window's 10,185 events; 52.6% of the corpus
Fitted on
cal_6, #1008

A map of the plottable half, and the frame says so. The sparse_geo caveat states the share that cannot be placed; coarse_geocode_precision explains the stray US toponyms (region names matching same-named places, tracked as #1043). It is not a claim about where the conflict is.

source_reliability_audit

15 of 44 sources

Which sources the corpus's own assertion history vindicates: a Bayesian reliability update, prior pseudo-count 80, for every source attribution resolves to.

Found
15 of 44 declared sources audited, 13 with evidence, 4 outliers flagged
Shrinkage
mean weight 0.8385, delta stdev 0.0449
Cohort
11.6% of the assertion history (16,067 of 138,989) resolves to a source; gdelt, the largest contributor, is outside it and keeps its starting value
Fitted on
cal_8, #1010

It scores the minority that attribution reaches and names the largest contributor it cannot score, instead of filling the gap with a default that would read as a score. The cohort widens only when the attribution backfill (#1015) reaches a re-ingested corpus.

narrative_shift_detection

69 of 573

Which narratives moved: windowed centroid drift of claim clusters against a date-shuffled null, 15-day windows, on sentence embeddings.

Found
69 narratives shift of 573 eligible, from 810 in the layer over 6,787 clustered claims
Confidence
0.517208 (coherence times source diversity)
Rate, not verdict
threshold is the 0.95 quantile of a permutation null, so about two in five detections are the expected false rate; a set is evidence, a single one is weak
Fitted on
cal_10, #1012, rule committed before the fitting code existed

Two warnings sit above the figure by design. The 45-day window cannot show a full emergence, peak and decline arc for most narratives (6.2% can), and the narrative layer exists in the snapshot only: 810 rows here, 0 in the production system of record until the operator write and projection rebuild.

gated: escalation_detection

gated, by construction

What an analyst sees when a capability's calibration block is switched off: a readable state with its reason, not an error and not a row that quietly disappears.

Endpoint
POST /api/v1/capabilities/escalation_detection/run → 409 capability_gated
Reason shown
"the escalation_detection block (version 1.0.0) is disabled"
How it was made
A scratch copy of the configuration with one block disabled, outside the repository. The published configuration was not touched.

A gate is a condition, not a disappearance. The point of the capture is that refusing to run is a state the interface can show, which is the same rule the Copilot follows when a question is outside the catalog.

The cluster hulls overlap heavily here. With this few relationship edges the layout leaves most actors unconnected, so each cluster's hull stretches across the canvas and the overlay reads as noise. The clustering underneath is sound -- the node table beside it lists the same assignments -- but the hull overlay needs denser edges than this corpus has to be worth looking at.

Flight-density coverage is crowd-sourced (ADS-B receivers) — an index of activity, not a census. An absent or zero value means no receiver coverage for that zone, NOT an absence of flights; do not read a missing/zero zone as no activity.

The window is the span the platform's acquisition and extraction pipeline processed end to end, so every figure describes the same corpus. Methods that take a window are pinned to it; methods that describe a single entity or trace one record are dated to the run instead.

The calibrated section was added on 25 August 2026 from the Tier-1 execution pass. The fitting records, the published configuration and the run report sit in the product repository and are available at the diligence tier.
